title: Meet Python
game_role: Your welcome screen is shown when the game starts.
objective: Print text with print() and use Python as a calculator
story: Hi! I'm Piko. Computers are very fast, but they don't know what to do on their own. You are going to tell them. Today we teach the computer to talk for the very first time!

sections.title: What is code?
sections.body:
Code is a list of instructions you give to a computer. Python reads these instructions **from top to bottom, line by line**, and carries them out in order.

Python is one of the most popular programming languages in the world. Games, websites, artificial intelligence... Python is everywhere.

sections.title: Talk with print()
sections.body:
`print()` writes whatever you put inside the parentheses on the screen. We put text **inside quotes**; numbers don't need quotes.

```python
print("Hello!")
print(42)
```

Use commas to print several things side by side. Python puts a space between them.

sections.title: Python is a calculator
sections.body:
- `+` addition, `-` subtraction
- `*` multiplication, `/` division
- `**` power: `2 ** 3` gives `8`

If you put a calculation inside quotes, Python doesn't calculate it, it prints it as it is: `print("2 + 2")` shows `2 + 2`.

sections.title: Comments and errors
sections.body:
Lines starting with `#` are **comments**. Python ignores them; you use them to leave notes for yourself.

If you mistype a letter, Python shows an error. Don't panic! The error message tells you which line the problem is on, and reading it carefully usually tells you what went wrong.

sections.title: Drawing on the stage: every star is a Piko
sections.body:
In some tasks, what you print **turns into a picture on the stage**. The rules are simple:

- `*` puts a **Piko** on the stage
- `#` is a **wall**, `o` is a **coin**, `H` is a **heart**
- a space is an empty square

So `print("***")` lines up three Pikos. Print it three times, one under another, and you have a 3-row Piko army!

examples.note: Run the code and look at the output.

examples.title: Let's calculate
examples.note: Why wasn't the last line calculated? Because it's inside quotes!

examples.title: Print with commas
examples.code:
# This is a comment, Python ignores it
print("Piko", "says:", "Hi!")
print("My age:", 12)

examples.note: Run it: five Pikos with five walls below them.

tasks.title: Your first words
tasks.prompt: Print exactly `Hello Python!` on the screen.
hints: Text must be inside quotes: print("...")
Capital letters and the exclamation mark must match too: Hello Python!

tasks.title: Introduce yourself
tasks.prompt: Print a sentence that starts with `My name is` and ends with your name. For example: `My name is Emma`
hints: Write "My name is" and your name inside the quotes.

tasks.title: How many hours in a year?
tasks.prompt: A year has 365 days and a day has 24 hours. Don't calculate it yourself; let Python do `365 * 24` and print the result.
hints: Don't put the calculation in quotes, or Python won't calculate it.

visual_task.title: Piko army
visual_task.prompt: Every `*` is a Piko on the stage. Use `print()` to line up an army of **3 rows** with **3 Pikos** in each row. Build the shape below!
hints: Write three print() lines for three rows.

challenge.title: Starry banner
challenge.prompt: Print a banner of at least 3 lines. At least 3 lines should contain `*`. A little secret: `print("*" * 20)` prints 20 stars side by side!
challenge.solution:
print("*" * 20)
print("*  PIKO IS COMING  *")
print("*" * 20)
hints: You can use three separate print() lines.

project_task.title: Welcome screen
project_task.prompt: Our game is called **Piko's Adventure**. Write the welcome screen shown when the game starts: print the game's name and the message `Welcome to the game!`. Decorate it with stars if you like.
project_task.solution:
print("*" * 30)
print("Piko's Adventure")
print("Welcome to the game!")
print("*" * 30)
hints: Write the text exactly as in the task.
